output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Composed Time Series}

In studies, we will often find it useful to construct functions that output the value of some variable over time. 
This package --- **`ramp.func`** --- has utilities to construct ***composed time series*** functions that are 
easy to manipulate. Each function is the product of four components: 

$$
x(t) = \bar x \times S(t) \times T(t) \times K(t)
$$

where

+ $\bar x$ is a scaling parameter to set the mean value over an interval $(t_0, t_1)$

+ $S(t)>0$ is a **seasonal** pattern function, normalized over the interval such that  $$\int_{t_0}^{t_1} S(t) \;dt = t_1 - t_0$$  

+ $T(t)>0$ is a **trend** pattern function, normalized over the interval such that $$\int_{t_0}^{t_1} T(t) \; dt = t_1 - t_0$$  

+ $K(t)>0$ is a **shock** function

The intent is to construct a function such that if $K(t)=1$, 
$$\int_{t_0}^{t_1} x(t) \; dt \approx \bar x.$$ 
Because of correlations between $S(t)$ and $T(t)$ there is no guarantee that the function will be equal to one.
